quiz.q: In a hazard and control table, what is the control for the 'cooking chicken' step?
quiz.explain: The hazard at cooking is bacteria surviving, and the control is reaching 70°C at the centre, checked with a probe.

quiz.q: Which pitch line is most specific and trustworthy?
options: 'We are the best caterers in town'
'Food is held above 60°C and we arrive one hour before serving'
quiz.explain: Specific, checkable details about safety and timing build trust more than general claims.

quiz.q: A client asks for 70 packs of Package A at ₦4,200 per head. What is the total?
Amaka wants to start selling bottled zobo in shops. Which body should she check with about product registration?
options: No one, it is not needed
quiz.explain: Packaged food products sold to the public generally need NAFDAC registration, and NAFDAC has guidance for small businesses.

quiz.q: During her capstone event the rice read 55°C on arrival. What should her capstone report do?
options: Leave it out to look professional
Record it honestly with the cause and the fix she will apply
quiz.explain: Honest records with corrective actions show real skill and protect guests next time.

quiz.q: A client asks to pay the balance after the party. What is the best reply?
options: Agree to keep the client happy
Politely explain that the balance is due before the event, as written in the terms
quiz.explain: Clear, consistent terms protect her from loss, and stating them politely keeps the relationship professional.

finalQuiz.q: Which list correctly gives the WHO Five Keys to Safer Food?
options: Keep clean; separate raw and cooked; cook thoroughly; keep food at safe temperatures; use safe water and raw materials
Keep clean; add salt; cook fast; cover food; serve early
Buy local; cook hot; serve cold; store dry; label all
finalQuiz.explain: These are WHO's five core messages for safe food handling.

finalQuiz.q: Rice is held in a cooler and reads 64°C at the venue. What does this mean?
options: It is in the danger zone and must be thrown away
It is above 60°C, so it is being held safely
finalQuiz.explain: Hot holding means keeping food above 60°C. At 64°C the rice is still safe to serve.

finalQuiz.q: Coleslaw for an event should be kept at which temperature?
options: Below 5°C, for example in a cooler with ice packs
finalQuiz.explain: Cold food should be held below 5°C because it is not cooked again before eating.

finalQuiz.q: How many birds does she need for 100 guests, one piece each, a 10% buffer and 8 pieces per bird?
finalQuiz.explain: 100 × 1.1 = 110 pieces, and 110 ÷ 8 = 13.75, so she buys 14 birds.

finalQuiz.q: A recipe for 10 uses 1 kg of tomato and pepper blend. How much for 100 guests?
finalQuiz.explain: The scaling factor is 100 ÷ 10 = 10, so 1 kg × 10 = 10 kg.

finalQuiz.q: When scaling a recipe 10 times, what should she do with salt and stock cubes?
options: Multiply exactly by 10 and never taste
Start with about three-quarters of the scaled amount, then taste and adjust
finalQuiz.explain: Seasoning does not always scale in a straight line, so add gradually and taste.

finalQuiz.q: Total job cost is ₦280,000 for 80 plates. What is the cost per plate?
Cost per plate is ₦3,500 and she wants a 30% margin. What is the price per plate, before rounding?
finalQuiz.explain: Price = ₦3,500 ÷ 0.70 = ₦5,000. A 30% markup would give ₦4,550, which is only about a 23% margin.

finalQuiz.q: A guest with a groundnut allergy is attending. Which plan is safest?
options: Remove the visible groundnuts from her plate
Cook her meal first in clean pots, seal and label it, and hand it to the host
Serve her from the general buffet
Tell her to pick out anything that looks like groundnut
finalQuiz.explain: Cooking first with clean equipment and sealing and labelling the pack prevents cross-contact.

finalQuiz.q: Serving is at 1:00 pm, set-up takes 45 minutes, travel 45 minutes and she wants a 30-minute buffer. When should she leave?
finalQuiz.explain: 1:00 pm minus 45 minutes set-up is 12:15 pm, minus 30 minutes buffer is 11:45 am arrival, minus 45 minutes travel is 11:00 am.

finalQuiz.q: A client books 100 packs at ₦4,200 each with a 50% deposit. How much is the deposit?
After four events she notices food often arrives below 60°C. What is the best next step?
options: Investigate the cause, for example preheat coolers, fill them fully or cook later, then re-test
Add more pepper to hide it
finalQuiz.explain: A repeated pattern points to a planning or equipment cause. Fixing and re-testing protects guests.

capstone.title: Catering Event Planning and Execution Project
capstone.brief: Plan, and if possible deliver, a catering job for a stated guest count (at least 30 guests). Produce a full event plan: client details, menu with portions, calculated quantities and shopping list, costing with price per head, a production timetable, a food safety plan with hazards, controls and logs, and a debrief.
steps: Choose a real or realistic client and record the event details, serving time, format and any allergies.
Write the menu with portion sizes and calculate quantities with a buffer.
Build the costing sheet, set your price per head and write a quotation with deposit terms.
Create a production timetable working backwards from serving time, plus an equipment checklist.
Write a food safety plan for the two highest-risk dishes and an allergy plan.
Deliver the event or do a test cook of at least one dish, filling temperature logs and taking photos.
Write a debrief: what went well, what went wrong, what you will change.
evidence: Menu with portion sizes and quantity calculations for the stated guest count
Costing sheet and quotation with deposit and balance terms
Food safety plan with hazard, control and check for each step of two dishes
Filled temperature and allergy logs with photos
Debrief notes and, for a real event, client feedback
